mainTopic: Green blood in the משנה (עקביא, the חכמים, רבי מאיר, רבי יוסי) and what 'like the blood of a wound' means for the impure red shade.
overview: This amud keeps working through the משנה about colors of blood. First the גמרא asks how עקביא בן מהללאל can call green blood טמא if the double word 'דמיה' teaches there are only four impure kinds. It answers that either he rejects that teaching, or green is just red that faded. It then explains that the חכמים differ from the תנא קמא, because the תנא קמא leaves other colors in doubt. Next it tries several readings of רבי מאיר's view and arrives at a גזרה שוה comparing her blood to water. The חכמים reject it, because nobody may make up a גזרה שוה on his own. The גמרא shows that רבי יוסי is really the תנא קמא, named so he gets credit. Finally it asks what 'like the blood of a wound' means and gives several models: a slaughtered ox, a living bird, a head louse, a young man's little finger, and bloodletting. A challenge to רב נחמן's bloodletting model begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the previous answer: the difference is about leaving blood in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The last word of the previous discussion. The difference between the earlier opinions is whether to leave certain blood colors in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: …to leave it in doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes the answer from the previous section of the גמרא. There, the difference between the תנא קמא and בית הלל was whether blood of certain colors is left as a ספק (doubt).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous section asked how בית הלל differ from the תנא קמא. The answer was that the תנא קמא treats extra colors as טמא only out of doubt, while בית הלל call them fully pure. This same idea comes back at the very end of this section.

keyTerms.meaning: To 'hang' or leave in doubt, treating something as uncertain instead of definitely טמא or טהור
Doubt, an uncertain status
Treated as impure only because of doubt

phrases.english: to leave in abeyance (as a doubt).
phrases.notes: This word finishes a sentence from just before this section. The difference between the opinions there is whether those colors stay in doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous section about the difference between the תנא קמא and בית הלל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical difference (נפקא מינה) between two opinions
steps.terutzMaskana: The two opinions differ on whether extra blood colors are treated as doubtful impurity or as fully pure.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: עקביא בן מהללאל says green blood is impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: עקביא בן מהללאל rules that green blood is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Green blood, עקביא בן מהללאל declares it impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to discuss it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed specific colors of blood that make a woman a נדה. עקביא בן מהללאל adds one more color, green, to the list of impure blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Green (or yellowish-green)
Declares impure

phrases.english: Green blood: Akavya ben Mahalalel deems it impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to עקביא בן מהללאל, green blood is טמא.

steps.title: Challenge: the verses teach only four kinds of impure blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether עקביא does not accept the teaching from the double 'דמיה', which limits impure blood to four kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't עקביא accept the teaching from 'her blood… her blood', that there are only four kinds here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עקביא's opinion. Earlier, two פסוקים that each say 'דמיה' were used to show there are exactly four kinds of impure blood, so how can he add green?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דמיה' (her bloods) is plural, so each use means two kinds, and two uses make four. The משנה lists five colors, but they count as only four kinds, because רבי חנינא says black is really red that has faded. So the four slots are already full. Adding green seems to break the limit of four.

keyTerms.meaning: Her bloods. The plural form is read as hinting at more than one kind of blood
He does not hold of (accept) this
Here there are four (kinds)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether green looks like blood. It is about a source from the פסוקים that seems to limit how many kinds of impure blood there can be.

phrases.english: But does Akavya not accept
'Her blood,' 'her blood': there are four here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of עקביא quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: עקביא's ruling that green blood is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The double 'דמיה' limits impure blood to four kinds. Adding green seems to go beyond that limit.

steps.title: First answer: עקביא does not accept that teaching
steps.stepSummary: One possible answer is that עקביא does not hold of the 'four kinds' teaching at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: he does not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first, simple answer. עקביא disagrees with the teaching from 'דמיה', so for him there can be more than four kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer removes the problem by saying the source does not bind עקביא. He simply does not read the פסוקים that way.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say… (introduces one of several possible answers)

phrases.english: If you wish, say: he does not accept it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the source applies to this תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone accepts that there are only four kinds of impure blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: עקביא does not accept that limit, so green can be a fifth kind.

steps.title: Second answer: green is red blood that faded
steps.stepSummary: Or עקביא does accept the 'four kinds' teaching. Green is not a new kind but red that changed color, just as רבי חנינא said about black.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say he does accept it. Didn't רבי חנינא say that black blood is really red, only it faded? Here too, the green is red that faded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that keeps the 'four kinds' teaching. Green blood is really red blood whose color faded, so it does not count as a new kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא already explained that the משנה's black blood is red that faded, so black does not add a kind. The גמרא uses the same idea for green. It falls under red, and the count stays at four.

keyTerms.meaning: He does hold of (accept) it
Black, one of the impure blood colors in the משנה
Was 'struck'. Here it means the color faded or was damaged
Here too, the same idea applies

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to defend עקביא. Either he rejects the 'four kinds' teaching, or he treats green as faded red, just like black, so it is not a new kind.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a changed color can still belong to the category of red blood. Its look changes, but its kind does not.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: he does accept it,
didn't Rabbi Ḥanina say:
Black is really red, only its color faded?
Here too, it is just that it has faded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same challenge, this time keeping the 'four kinds' teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: green falls under an existing kind (red)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Green is a separate, fifth kind of blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Green is red blood that faded, so it does not add to the four kinds.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the חכמים say green is pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next words: the חכמים rule green blood pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: And the חכמים declare it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the חכמים' reply to עקביא in the משנה. It is setting up a question about their opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים disagree with עקביא and say green blood does not make a woman טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view in the משנה)
Declare pure

phrases.english: And the Rabbis deem it pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the משנה, which answer עקביא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, green blood is טהור.

steps.title: Challenge: the חכמים seem to say the same as the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים are mentioned at all, since the תנא קמא already listed only certain colors as impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the חכמים' opinion. The תנא קמא already left green off the list of impure colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא's list did not include green, then the תנא קמא also holds that green is not impure. So the חכמים seem to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as…
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: This is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the חכמים' statement quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra statement of the חכמים in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנא קמא already left green off the impure list, so the חכמים' ruling seems repetitive.

steps.title: Answer: they differ on whether green is left in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The difference is that the תנא קמא leaves other colors such as green in doubt, while the חכמים call green fully pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: whether to leave it in doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions are not the same. The תנא קמא treats green as a ספק, possibly impure, while the חכמים say it is definitely pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, only the listed colors are surely impure. Other colors are not declared pure, only doubtful. The חכמים go further and declare green fully טהור, so their statement adds a real halachic difference.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them (a practical outcome where they disagree)
Definitely pure, with no doubt

steps.whatToRemember: Leaving a color off a list does not always mean it is pure. The תנא קמא leaves green in doubt, while the חכמים call it fully pure.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that 'not on the impure list' means 'pure'. For the תנא קמא it means 'doubtful'.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: whether to leave it in abeyance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7, using the same idea as step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical difference (נפקא מינה) between two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים and the תנא קמא hold exactly the same view on green blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא leaves green in doubt, while the חכמים declare it fully pure.

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר's words in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of רבי מאיר's statement about green blood in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: 'Even if it does not make impure as a stain,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the next line of the משנה, where רבי מאיר speaks about green blood. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says that even if green blood does not make a woman impure as a כתם, it still counts as a liquid. As a liquid, it can make food able to become impure. The גמרא now wants to understand what רבי מאיר really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on clothing or another object, not seen coming out of the body
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the quoted line continues

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
"If it does not make impure because of a stain," etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the line in the משנה says it is still impure as a liquid, so it can make food able to become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the חכמים's ruling (steps 6-8) to the next opinion in the משנה, רבי מאיר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if green blood does not make impure as a כתם, it is still impure as a liquid.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: רבי מאיר agreed with עקביא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר holds that green blood seen coming from the body is impure. Only a green stain found on clothing is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי מאיר accepted the view of עקביא בן מהללאל and ruled it impure. This is what he told the רבנן: Granted that when a woman finds a green stain on a garment, you don't make her impure. But when she sees green blood coming from her own body, she should be impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains רבי מאיר's words. He says רבי מאיר really sided with עקביא that green blood can make a woman impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר makes a split. A green stain on clothing is pure, because we are not sure it came from her body. Green blood she sees leaving her body is impure. So the phrase 'not impure as a stain' is only about stains.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Went down to the approach of', meaning he adopted someone else's opinion
'Granted', admitting one point before arguing another
Green blood
On a garment or piece of clothing

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: יָרַד רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְשִׁיטַת עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir went over to the approach of Akavya ben Mahalalel,
phrases.notes: עקביא is the one in the משנה who rules that green blood is impure.

phrases.english: and ruled it impure.
And this is what he was saying to the Rabbis:
Granted that where she finds
a green stain on a garment, you do not rule her impure,
but where she sees green blood from her body,
she should be impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יָרַד רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְשִׁיטַת עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה line quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Green blood seen from the body is impure, as עקביא holds. A green stain on clothing is pure.

steps.title: Then why did רבי מאיר speak about a liquid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רבי מאיר holds that seen green blood makes her impure, why did he mention only that it is impure as a liquid?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why did he say 'if it is not impure as a stain, it is impure as a liquid'? He should have said it makes her impure because she saw it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's explanation. It uses רבי מאיר's own wording in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If seen green blood makes the woman a נדה, that is a much stronger point than 'it counts as a liquid.' רבי מאיר should have said the strong point: she is impure because she saw it. Since he only mentioned the liquid point, it seems he did not hold she becomes a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so', the opening of a challenge to an explanation
A liquid, here one that makes food able to become impure
A woman who sees blood come from her body, which makes her a נדה
'He should have said', meaning a better wording was expected

phrases.english: If so,
"if it does not make impure because of a stain,
it makes impure because of a liquid"?
He should have said: because she saw it!
phrases.notes: He means: say she is impure as a נדה, because she saw the blood come from her body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אִם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם, מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם מַשְׁקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's explanation from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי מאיר holds seen green blood makes her impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's wording mentions only the weaker 'liquid' impurity. If he held she becomes a נדה, he should have said so.

steps.title: Green blood that comes after red blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reading. Green blood seen from the start is pure. Green blood seen after red blood is impure, like the liquids of a זב and זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he told them: Granted that when she sees green blood from the start, you don't make her impure. But when she saw red blood and then saw green blood, she should be impure. It is just like the liquids of a זב and a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the earlier reading with a new explanation of רבי מאיר. This new reading fits his 'liquid' wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי מאיר agrees that green blood alone does not make a woman a נדה. But once she is already impure from red blood, the green blood counts as a liquid coming from an impure person. Every liquid from a זב or זבה is impure, so this green blood is impure as a liquid too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, this is what he meant', introducing a new reading
From the start, with nothing before it
'Just as it is with', comparing to a known law
A man or woman with an impure discharge. All liquids from their body are impure

steps.whatToRemember: In this reading, רבי מאיר holds that green blood alone does not make a woman a נדה, but green blood that comes after red blood is impure as a liquid, like the liquids of a זב or זבה. The גמרא sets this reading aside in step 14 and offers a new one in step 15.
steps.confusionAlert: This green blood does not make her a נדה by itself. It is impure only as a liquid coming from someone who is already impure.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he was saying to them:

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי הֵיכָא דְּקָא חָזְיָא דָּם יָרוֹק מֵעִיקָּרָא
phrases.english: Granted that where she sees green blood from the start,
you do not rule her impure,
but where she saw red blood
and then saw green blood,
she should be impure,
just as it is with the liquids of a zav and a zavah.
phrases.notes: Liquids that come from a זב or זבה, like spit or urine, are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by setting aside רבי יוחנן's case split and offering a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the statement. The case split moves from 'stain versus seen' to 'green alone versus green after red.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר holds that green blood seen from the body makes her a נדה (רבי יוחנן's reading).
steps.terutzMaskana: Green blood alone is pure. Green blood after red is impure as a liquid, like the liquids of a זב or זבה. This fits the 'liquid' wording.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: only fluids that gather and flow out like saliva are impure
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים explain why green blood is not like saliva. Saliva gathers and then comes out. Green blood does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? They say: the impure fluids must be like saliva. Just as saliva gathers and then comes out, so too only fluids that gather and come out are impure. This leaves out green blood, which does not gather and come out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר compared green blood that comes after red to the liquids of a זב or זבה, which are all impure. The גמרא now gives the חכמים' answer: only fluids like saliva count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים agree that saliva is impure, but they say saliva is the model for which fluids count. A fluid must gather inside and then come out the way saliva does. Green blood does not behave that way, so the comparison fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, like
Saliva
Gathers together and comes out
To exclude, to leave out

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? Similar to saliva:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how the חכמים answer רבי מאיר's comparison of green blood to the liquids of a זב or זבה.

phrases.english: just as saliva gathers and comes out,
so too anything that gathers and comes out,
to exclude this, which does not gather and come out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' reply to רבי מאיר's saliva comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the category narrowly so the case falls outside it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Green blood after red should be impure like all the liquids of a זב or זבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only fluids that gather and flow out like saliva are impure; green blood is excluded.

steps.title: If so, the חכמים are right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the חכמים' answer is convincing. So why would רבי מאיר still argue?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the חכמים spoke well to רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the חכמים' answer is so strong that it is hard to see how רבי מאיר could disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר's whole argument was the comparison to the liquids of a זב or זבה, the חכמים fully answered it with the saliva rule. This means we must have misunderstood what רבי מאיר was saying, so the גמרא will look for a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
They spoke well; their answer is correct

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: the Rabbis spoke well to Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of רבי מאיר that step 13 answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation (step 12) that רבי מאיר compared green blood after red to the liquids of a זב or זבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים' reply is so convincing that רבי מאיר could not reasonably keep his view if that were his argument.

steps.title: רבי מאיר meant: green blood should at least make seeds susceptible
steps.stepSummary: A new reading: רבי מאיר said green blood should at least count as a liquid that makes seeds able to become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he was saying to them: let it at least be like a liquid that makes seeds able to become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new explanation of רבי מאיר's argument. He was not comparing to saliva, but to the liquids that make food able to become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become impure after it gets wet from one of the special liquids. רבי מאיר is saying green blood should at least count as one of those liquids. This is a smaller claim than calling it impure like the fluids of a זב or זבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid
To make food able to become impure
Seeds, produce

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he was saying to them:
let it be like a liquid that makes seeds susceptible.
phrases.notes: Food can only become impure after it gets wet from certain liquids; he wants green blood to be one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by re-reading רבי מאיר's argument.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר compared green blood after red to the liquids of a זב or זבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר said green blood should at least make food susceptible to impurity.

steps.title: The חכמים require 'blood of the slain'
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that only blood like 'blood of the slain' makes food susceptible, and green blood is not like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים require 'blood of the slain,' and this is not that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the חכמים' answer to the new reading of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים learn from a פסוק that the blood which makes food susceptible must be like blood that flows when someone is killed. Green blood is not that kind of blood, so it does not make food susceptible.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires
Blood of the slain
It is not there; it is missing

phrases.english: And the Rabbis require 'blood of the slain,' and it is not that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' reply to the second reading of רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses a פסוק to limit the category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Green blood should make food susceptible like other liquids.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only blood like 'blood of the slain' makes food susceptible; green blood does not.

steps.title: Again, the חכמים seem right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats its challenge: the חכמים' answer is convincing, so why would רבי מאיר disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the חכמים spoke well to רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same challenge again against the second reading of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים have a פסוק on their side. If רבי מאיר had no source of his own, he could not argue. So the גמרא needs a third reading that gives רבי מאיר a real source.

keyTerms.meaning: They were saying to him
The חכמים, the majority of the sages

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר!
phrases.english: the Rabbis spoke well to Rabbi Meir!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second reading answered in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי מאיר simply wanted green blood to make food susceptible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים' פסוק answers that claim fully, so רבי מאיר would have no basis to argue.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns it from a גזרה שוה
steps.stepSummary: Third reading: רבי מאיר has a גזרה שוה linking the woman's discharge to water, which makes food susceptible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he was saying to them: learn it from a גזרה שוה. It says here 'Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates,' and it says there 'and sends water upon the fields.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי מאיר a real source: a גזרה שוה from a shared word in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the word 'send' (שלח). One describes the woman's discharge, the other describes water. Since water makes food susceptible, רבי מאיר says her blood, even green blood, does too.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn it
Learning a law from the same word in two פסוקים
Your shoots, your sendings
And sends water

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he was saying to them:
learn it from a verbal analogy,
it is written here: 'Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates,'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 4:13. The גמרא reads this as a hint to the woman's discharge.

phrases.english: and it is written there:
'and sends water upon the fields.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ: אַלְּפוּהָ בִּגְזֵרָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by giving רבי מאיר a source from the פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Provides a scriptural source for the speaker
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר had no source strong enough to stand against the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר relies on a גזרה שוה comparing the woman's blood to water.

steps.title: The חכמים: no one may make up a גזרה שוה on his own
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the גזרה שוה because a person may make a קל וחומר on his own, but not a גזרה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? A person may derive a קל וחומר on his own, but a person may not derive a גזרה שוה on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the חכמים do not accept רבי מאיר's גזרה שוה, and this closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר is plain logic, so anyone may use it. A גזרה שוה must come from a tradition handed down from one's teachers. The חכמים did not receive this one, so they do not accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
Derives, learns out
On his own, without a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds green blood makes food susceptible because of a גזרה שוה. The חכמים reject it because a גזרה שוה needs a tradition, while a קל וחומר does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule across ש״ס: a גזרה שוה can only be used if it was received from one's teachers.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
A person may derive an a fortiori inference on his own,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אָדָם דָּן גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה מֵעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: but a person may not derive a verbal analogy on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם דָּן קַל וָחוֹמֶר מֵעַצְמוֹ, וְאֵין אָדָם דָּן גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה מֵעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' reply to רבי מאיר's גזרה שוה, ending the back-and-forth.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the source using a general rule of learning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזרה שוה should bind the חכמים too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים have no tradition for this גזרה שוה, so they do not accept it.

steps.title: רבי יוסי seems to repeat the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי from the משנה and asks why he is needed, since the תנא קמא already said the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: 'Neither this way nor that way.' But that is exactly what the תנא קמא said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's line from the משנה about green blood and asks why the משנה needs it. The anonymous first opinion already ruled the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already treats green blood as not counting as blood. רבי יוסי says green blood counts neither as נדה blood nor as a liquid that makes food able to become impure. Since nothing seems new, the גמרא asks why his words are there.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
That is the same as (used to point out an apparent repetition)
Neither this way nor that way

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Neither this way, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line is 'neither this way nor that way': green blood isn't impure as נדה blood, and it doesn't make food able to become impure.

phrases.english: That is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the long back-and-forth about רבי מאיר and the חכמים, the גמרא turns to the last opinion in that part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement that only repeats an earlier ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רבי יוסי is the תנא קמא, named to give him credit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is teaching that the anonymous first opinion belongs to רבי יוסי. Saying a teaching in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: Who is the תנא קמא? רבי יוסי. And anyone who says something in the name of the person who said it brings redemption to the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not adding a new opinion. It is telling us who the anonymous first opinion belongs to: רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition is not a second ruling. It identifies the author. Naming him is worth it because quoting a teaching בשם אומרו has great value, so the 'extra' words are there on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is teaching us
In the name of the one who said it
Redemption

steps.whatToRemember: The anonymous opinion about green blood is really רבי יוסי's. He is named because giving credit to the one who said a teaching brings redemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known teaching about giving proper credit when quoting a teaching.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
Who is the first tanna? Rabbi Yosei,
and anyone who says something in the name of the one who said it
brings redemption to the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: מַאן תַּנָּא קַמָּא? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the author of the anonymous opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's statement looked like a pointless repeat of the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It shows that the תנא קמא is רבי יוסי, named so that he gets credit.

steps.title: What does 'like the blood of a wound' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's definition of the red shade and asks what 'כדם המכה' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What counts as red? Like the blood of a wound. What does 'like the blood of a wound' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, which defines the impure red color. It asks for the exact meaning of 'like the blood of a wound.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood from a wound comes in many shades, so the משנה's description is unclear. The גמרא needs a precise reference shade to know which red is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Red, one of the impure colors of blood
Blood from a wound or a blow

phrases.english: What is red?
Like the blood of a wound.
What does 'like the blood of a wound' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזֶהוּ אָדוֹם כְּדַם הַמַּכָּה. מַאי כְּדַם הַמַּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, the shades of blood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact shade meant by 'like the blood of a wound'

steps.title: שמואל: like the blood of a slaughtered ox
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, explains that it means the blood of a slaughtered ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: like the blood of a slaughtered ox.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by giving a clear model to compare against: the blood of an ox that was just slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general phrase 'a wound' is replaced with one specific case. That gives a fixed shade for judging whether blood is impure red.

keyTerms.meaning: A slaughtered ox

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
Like the blood of a slaughtered ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּדַם שׁוֹר שָׁחוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shade of blood from a slaughtered ox

steps.title: Then why not just say 'like the blood of slaughter'?
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל is right, the משנה should have said 'like the blood of slaughter' directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it say 'like the blood of slaughter'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's reading. If the משנה meant slaughter, why did it use the word 'wound'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה meant שחיטה, the clearer word would have been 'slaughter.' Its choice of 'wound' seems to argue against שמואל's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But let it say (the משנה should have worded it this way)
Kosher slaughter

phrases.english: Then let it say 'like the blood of slaughter'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's explanation in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading of 'כדם המכה' as slaughter blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If slaughter was meant, the משנה would have used the more direct word.

steps.title: 'Wound' points to the first cut of the knife
steps.stepSummary: 'Slaughter' could mean blood from the whole process. 'Wound' shows it means only the blood at the very first cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had said 'like the blood of slaughter,' I would think it means the blood of the whole slaughter. So it teaches us 'like the blood of a wound': like the beginning of the knife's cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. The word 'wound' was chosen on purpose, to point to the blood at the very start of the cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood changes shade during the slaughter. 'Slaughter' could cover any of those shades. 'Wound' narrows it to the first blood that comes out when the knife strikes.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (the mistaken first assumption)
A blow or cut
Knife

phrases.english: If it had said 'like the blood of slaughter,'
I would have thought: like the whole slaughter,
phrases.notes: He means any of the blood that comes out during the whole slaughter, whatever its shade.

phrases.english: so it teaches us 'like the blood of a wound':
like the beginning of the knife's cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמַר כְּדַם שְׁחִיטָה הֲוָה אָמֵינָא כְּכוּלַּהּ שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the משנה chose its wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Slaughter' would have meant any blood from the whole slaughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Wound' means only the first blood at the start of the cut.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, impure red is like the first blood of a freshly slaughtered ox, at the moment the knife first cuts.

steps.title: עולא: like the blood of a living bird
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives a different model for the red shade: the blood of a living bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא says: like the blood of a living bird.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a second explanation of 'like the blood of a wound.' It means blood from a living bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a slaughtered ox, עולא compares the red to a living bird's blood. That is a different reference shade, and his word 'living' raises a question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A living bird

phrases.english: Ulla says:
Like the blood of a living bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the question of step 22, different from שמואל's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The impure red is like the blood of a living bird.

steps.title: What does 'living' rule out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'living' rules out a slaughtered bird or a weak bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: 'Living' to rule out a slaughtered bird, or perhaps to rule out a weak one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what עולא meant by 'living.' It sets up two possible meanings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Living' could mean not slaughtered, so slaughter blood is ruled out. It could also mean healthy and strong, so a weak bird is ruled out. Each reading gives a different reference shade.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked (an open question was raised)
To rule out, to exclude
Perhaps
Weak, thin

phrases.english: They asked:
Does 'living' rule out a slaughtered bird,
or perhaps it rules out a weak one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: חַיָּה לְאַפּוֹקֵי שָׁחוּט, אוֹ דִּלְמָא לְאַפּוֹקֵי כָּחוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of a word in עולא's statement in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'living' rules out a slaughtered bird or a weak bird

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle what 'living' rules out. It ends the question with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither reading of עולא is proven. The exact meaning of 'living bird' stays unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to understand 'like the blood of a wound'. שמואל says the first blood of a slaughtered ox. עולא says the blood of a living bird, and what 'living' rules out is left unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 27 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether עולא's 'living' rules out a slaughtered bird or a weak bird remains undecided.

steps.title: Red like the blood of a head louse
steps.stepSummary: זעירי quotes רבי חנינא: the red shade is like the blood of a louse from the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא: the red is like the blood of a louse from the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another opinion about which red the משנה means. רבי חנינא compares it to the blood of a squashed head louse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא compared the red to the blood of a living bird. רבי חנינא gives a different model, and he is specific: a louse from the head, not from anywhere on the body. That detail is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A louse (literally 'a biter')
Like the blood of
Of the head

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
Like the blood of a louse of the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the open question about עולא's bird, a new model for the red shade is offered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The red of impure blood matches the blood of a head louse.

steps.title: A louse from anywhere on the body?
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a woman who killed a louse may blame a stain on it. That seems to mean a louse from any part of her body, not only the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'If she killed a louse, she may blame the stain on it.' Doesn't this mean a louse from her whole body?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא from a משנה about blood stains. The משנה allows a woman to blame a stain on a louse she killed, and it does not say 'from the head.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the louse is a reason to explain the stain away, louse blood must look like the blood we are worried about. If any louse on the body counts, then the red shade should be 'louse blood' in general. That would make רבי חנינא's limit to the head seem wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: She killed
She may attribute (blame the stain on something else and stay pure)
Is it not so that...? (opens a challenging reading)
Her body

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If she killed a louse,
she may attribute [the stain] to it.
phrases.notes: This comes from a later משנה about stains; she blames the stain on the louse and stays pure.

phrases.english: Is it not [speaking of a louse] from her whole body?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי חנינא's limit to a head louse.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's statement that the model is specifically a head louse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה about stains mentions a louse with no limit, which suggests a louse from anywhere on the body.

steps.title: The משנה means a louse from her head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a louse that was on her head.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means a louse from her head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חנינא by reading the משנה narrowly: the louse she killed was on her head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not have to mean any louse at all. Read as a head louse, it fits רבי חנינא perfectly, and the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the suggested reading)
Of her head

phrases.english: No, [a louse] of her head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the louse case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to mean a louse from anywhere on her body.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a head louse, which matches רבי חנינא.

steps.title: Red like a young man's re-wounded little finger
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains 'like the blood of a wound': blood from the little finger that was wounded, healed and wounded again, of an unmarried young man up to age twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמי ורדינאה said in the name of רבי אבהו: it is like the blood of the little finger of the hand that was wounded, healed and wounded again. Not any person's finger, only that of a young man who has not married. Up to what age? Up to twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a very exact model for the red shade. רבי אבהו describes the exact finger, the exact kind of wound, and the exact person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each condition narrows down the shade: the little finger, a second wound on a healed spot, and an unmarried young man no older than twenty. These details matter because the next step tests whether real cases in the משנה can fit them.

keyTerms.meaning: The little finger
Was wounded (bruised)
Healed (literally 'came back to life')
A young man
Married a woman

phrases.english: Ami of Vardina said in the name of Rabbi Abbahu:
Like the blood of the little finger of the hand,
that was wounded and healed,
and was then wounded again.
And not the finger of every person,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁל בָּחוּר שֶׁלֹּא נָשָׂא אִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: but that of a young man who has not married a woman.
And up to what age? Up to twenty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the louse model is defended, a new model for 'the blood of a wound' is offered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The red matches blood from a re-wounded little finger of an unmarried young man up to age twenty.

steps.title: How can a husband be unmarried?
steps.stepSummary: A משנה lets a woman blame a stain on her son or her husband. A son can be young and unmarried, but a husband is married by definition.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'She may blame the stain on her son or on her husband.' With her son, fine, that can happen. But her husband, how can that happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו from the stains משנה. It allows blaming a stain on a wounded husband, but רבי אבהו's model needs an unmarried man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stain can be blamed on the husband's wound, his blood must look like the red shade in question. A son can easily be under twenty and unmarried. But a husband seems to always be married, so he should never match רבי אבהו's model.

keyTerms.meaning: Her son
Her husband
Granted, this part works...
You can find such a case
How?

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
She may attribute [the stain] to her son or to her husband.
phrases.notes: The same stains משנה: if her son or husband was wounded, she blames the stain on him and stays pure.

phrases.english: Granted, with her son, you can find such a case,
but with her husband,
how can you find such a case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי אבהו's 'unmarried young man' condition against the stains משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's condition that the model is an unmarried young man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets her blame the stain on her husband, but a husband is married and so cannot fit the model.

steps.title: A husband after the חופה but before being together
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers: the case is where she entered the חופה but they have not yet been intimate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: for example, where she entered the חופה but they had not yet been together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבהו by finding a husband who still counts as 'not married' for this purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters for רבי אבהו is that the man has not yet been with a woman. A husband right after the חופה, before they have been together, is legally her husband but physically like an unmarried young man. So the משנה's case of the husband fits.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as
The marriage canopy
She was intimate with her husband

steps.whatToRemember: Two more models for the red shade: a head louse (רבי חנינא) and a young unmarried man's re-wounded little finger (רבי אבהו). Each one was defended by reading the stains משנה narrowly: a louse from her head, and a husband after the חופה before they were together.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
For example, where she entered the marriage canopy,
but they had not yet been together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה לַחוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the husband.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a specific case that fits the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A husband is always married, so he could never match רבי אבהו's model.
steps.terutzMaskana: A husband who has entered the חופה but has not yet been with his wife still fits the 'unmarried young man' model.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the red is like blood from bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains the red color of טמא blood as the color of blood that flows during bloodletting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says: the red is like the blood of bloodletting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers his own explanation of the red shade of טמא blood. He says it looks like blood let out during bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו compared the red to blood from a small, re-opened wound on a young unmarried man's little finger. רב נחמן picks a different, more familiar example: the blood that comes out when someone has blood drawn. Both are trying to pin down the exact shade the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: Bloodletting, drawing blood from the body as a medical treatment
Like the blood of bloodletting, רב נחמן's measure for the red shade

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying that blood from bloodletting makes a woman טמאה. He is only using its color as a sample to show what the red shade looks like.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman says:
Like the blood of bloodletting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives yet another explanation of the red color, after those of שמואל, עולא, רבי חנינא and רבי אבהו (steps 23-32).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The red of טמא blood matches the color of blood drawn during bloodletting.

steps.title: A challenge begins from an incident with רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן: an incident where רבי מאיר attributed a stain to some cause.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: There was an incident, and רבי מאיר attributed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רב נחמן. It begins quoting a ברייתא about a real incident where רבי מאיר blamed a stain on something, and the story continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיתיבי tells us a source is coming that seems to contradict what was just said. So far we only hear that רבי מאיר 'attributed' a stain to something. We have to wait for the rest of the ברייתא to see exactly how it clashes with רב נחמן's bloodletting comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a real case that happened
He attributed or blamed (a stain on some other cause, so the woman stays טהורה)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
There was an incident, and Rabbi Meir attributed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רב נחמן's definition in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's statement that the red shade is like blood of bloodletting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about an incident where רבי מאיר attributed a stain will be shown to contradict רב נחמן's comparison. The details continue in the next part of the text.
